document.title: Afghanistan: Heavy Fighting Rages West of Kabul; Herat Calm After Taliban Take-Over
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] The Taliban take Herat, forcing Ismail Khan and 300-600 followers into Iran. Hekmatyar's forces are attacked by Masoud's government troops. A crowd set fire to the Pakistani Embassy in Kabul in response to Pakistan's support for the Taliban.

events.description: Taliban took Herat, declared a three-day holiday; Ismael Khan fled toward Iran.
Taliban attacked Masood's positions west of Kabul at Company; Masood counter-attacked Sher Alam.
Rabbani chaired an emergency meeting on reaction to loss of Herat.
Heavy fighting between Jamiat and Hekmatyar commander Zardad on route to Jalalabad.
Reported mob attack and fire at Pakistani embassy in Kabul blaming Islamabad for fall of Herat.
Masood Khalili told US poloff Rabbani supports UN/OIC effort.
Taliban take Herat and declare a three-day holiday.
Ismael Khan flees Taybat for Mashhad and is disarmed by Iranian border officials.
Taliban at Maidan Shahr attack Masood's positions west of Kabul.
Sher Alam defects to the Taliban.
Rabbani chairs emergency meeting on the loss of Herat.
Masood Khalili briefs US embassy on Rabbani's position.
False rumor of Baba Jan coup against Rabbani.
Heavy fighting between Jamiat forces and Zardad over the road to Jalalabad.
Commander Basir announces defection to Dostam in Badakhshan.
Dostam's forces under Rasul Pahlawan take Torghundi.
Reports of mob setting fire to the Pakistani Embassy in Kabul blaming Islamabad for Herat's fall.

key_claims: The Taliban captured Herat on 4 September 1995 and the city remained calm.
Ismael Khan fled to Mashhad, Iran, where he was disarmed by Iranian border officials.
Masood's military remained the most capable force in Afghanistan, though defections and divisions with Rabbani were noted.
Kabul acknowledged the Rabbani formula would now give opposition a majority of provincial seats.
Dostam's Jumbesh forces took Torghundi but were told to avoid engaging the Taliban.
A mob attacked the Pakistani embassy in Kabul blaming Islamabad for Herat's fall.
